findings.evidence: Wrapper v2 and executor v1 bytes at HEAD are identical to the cycle-02 reviewed head, so the path-based packed-payload immutability window, the ungated importability of executor.reconstruct, the stale authoritative_execution_code_head metadata field, the import-before-hash-verify module ordering, and the missing outputs-directory term in the PRIOR_STATE conjunction persist exactly as dispositioned. All five require an out-of-threat-model adversarial local writer or manual interference, none can mint authority (expected-S1 sha equality alone confers authority; mismatch_never_acquires_authority), and each fails closed or yields a truthful consumed-failure record.

findings.title: The eight-field go-token has no nonce or attempt-state binding, so token replay is prevented by the durable PRIOR_STATE gate rather than by the token itself
findings.evidence: The token is a pure function of (approval bytes, release bytes, ids, disposition). A second --execute with the same token fails closed pre-attempt at PRIOR_STATE because the first attempt's state directory durably persists in every outcome. Only manual deletion of the release-private state tree under ~/.local/share/pulsarmlx/... could re-open the gate, which is the same manual-interference class already dispositioned as defense in depth in cycle 02 (S1MAT-R2-F3), and even then the replayed event could only reproduce the identical expected-sha-gated S1 bytes with ledger 175-to-175 and zero checkpoint/shard access.
findings.required_action: May remain with justification. Optionally include a single-use nonce or the attempt-start sha in a future token schema.

final_question_answer: YES. The committed approval at docs/architecture/reviews/evidence/f017-representative-s1-materialization-single-use-release-v2-independent-approval-v1.json (sha256 e2729bb1c8aee5ef8cc1b9920bfa832c4eb2ffcb72b782e8df20af1698f36108, byte-identical from its approval-bearing head fe644ce through reviewed head 469aefd9) is sufficient for a later machine-local token readiness phase without executing or materializing S1. It is exactly the 18-field document the sha-bound wrapper v2 authorize() gate demands — verified field-set-exact with no missing or extra keys and every value constraint satisfied against live committed bytes — and it pins, directly or through exact sha256 chains re-verified this cycle, the release v2 (c441f956...), the authorization (f2efce04...), the ACCEPT cycle-02 release review by claude-fable-5 at f0165acd (bd56546e..., whose reviewed bytes equal HEAD bytes for every bound artifact), all 13 execution-code and data bindings, the expected S1 identity 8309377e..., ledger 175-to-175, zero-checkpoint/zero-shard accounting, and the stop boundary AFTER_REPRESENTATIVE_S1_RETENTION_ONLY. The chain release -> review -> approval -> machine-local token is acyclic and fail-closed; the approval executes nothing and is not a token (both declared and structurally enforced: the go-token is absent, the release-2 machine-local root does not exist, and --execute today fails at APPROVAL_OR_TOKEN_ABSENT before any state); the superseded release v1 cannot satisfy the v2 gate in either direction; and a future token equal to exactly the eight bound fields can authorize at most one S1 materialization, after which durable attempt state permanently closes the gate. No BLOCKING and no NON_BLOCKING_REQUIRED findings remain; the two recorded observations are justified defense in depth. VERDICT: ACCEPT.
